Pond excavation in Brahmanbaria uncovers mortar shell believed to be from Liberation War
2026-03-30T18:40:34+06:00 | Our Correspondent, Brahmanbaria
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/pond-excavation-brahmanbaria-uncovers-mortar-shell-believed-be-liberation-war-4139246

A live mortar shell, believed to date back to the 1971 Liberation War, was unearthed during the excavation of a pond in Brahmanbaria Sadar upazila.

The shell was discovered around 1:00pm yesterday in Borohoron village under Dakkhin Natai union, when local workers were digging soil for the pond.

According to police and local sources, the shell was recovered from the house of Farid Uddin Ahmed, a Language Movement veteran and former president of the Brahmanbaria Chamber of Commerce.

Upon receiving news, police rushed to the scene and cordoned off the area with ropes to ensure safety. A team from the Bangladesh Army visited the site this noon.

Army officials said an artillery shell disposal unit from Cumilla Cantonment will defuse the shell.

Police suspect the shell had remained buried since the Liberation War.

Emdadul Bari, a resident of the house, said the pond was being excavated after about four decades.

“During the Liberation War, Pakistani forces had set up a camp at our abandoned house. Many Pakistani soldiers were killed here in direct clashes with the freedom fighters. We believe the mortar shell might have landed here during that time,” he added.

Meanwhile, as news of the mortar shell recovery spread, people of all ages, including children and teenagers, gathered at the site from nearby areas. To prevent any accident, the police cordoned off the entire area and urged the public to maintain a safe distance.
